import numpy as np

# Create a boolean mask of non-null values
non_null_mask = df.notnull()

# For each column, find the first non-null value in each row
first_non_null = df.where(non_null_mask).bfill(axis=1)

# For each column, find the last null position in each row
last_null_pos = non_null_mask.cumsum(axis=1).sub(non_null_mask.shape[1]).abs().mul(-1).sub(1)
last_null_pos = last_null_pos.where(last_null_pos.ge(0)).fillna(-1).astype(int)

# Create an output DataFrame initialized with NaNs
result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=df.index, columns=df.columns)

# Fill the values by placing each row's non-null values at the end of the row
for col in df.columns:
    col_pos = df.columns.get_loc(col)
    # For each row, if this column position is a null position, fill with the corresponding value
    valid_rows = last_null_pos.eq(col_pos)
    result.loc[valid_rows, col] = first_non_null.loc[valid_rows, col]

# For columns that should remain unchanged (where no nulls exist), copy original values
result.update(df.where(non_null_mask))

j = tf.range(tf.size(b), dtype=tf.int32))

# Flatten and stack indices
indices = tf.stack([tf.repeat(i, tf.shape(b)), tf.tile(j, [tf.shape(a)[0], 1])], axis=-1)
# Gather elements from a and b based on indices
a_vals = tf.gather(a, indices[:, 0])
b_vals = tf.gather(b, indices[:, 1])
# Stack to form the cartesian product
result = tf.stack([a_vals, b_vals], axis=-1)
